subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood + Finovate — stakeholder mapping & champion enablement
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finovatebank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood + Finovate — stakeholder mapping & next steps

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from today:

1) What we heard (short):
- Primary use: realtime risk-scoring and customer support automation for retail lending
- Traffic profile: ~600k queries/month, 95th pct latency target ~150ms server-side
- Primary constraints: data locality (US-only), SOC 2 evidence, procurement approval timeline

2) Key decision criteria you mentioned:
- Cost per 1M tokens / predictable unit economics
- SLA-backed latency targets and dedicated capacity options
- Security/compliance paperwork (SOC 2, data residency, audit logs)
- Exec-level ROI: quantifiable reduction in manual review and NPS improvement

3) Asks / next steps:
- Can you share the names/emails for: economic buyer (finance/ops), security lead, procurement contact, and anyone who will review legal terms?
- Procurement timeline: when would you need vendor quotes / PO?
- Security: will they want an architecture diagram and SOC 2 summary?

Attachments: redwood-inference-platform-overview.pdf, procurement-worksheet.xlsx (our template for procurement asks)

If you can send the stakeholder list, I’ll assemble a short champion enablement packet (talk tracks + ROI bullets) Alex can use for internal briefings. I’d also recommend a 30-minute follow-up next week to align the mutual action plan.

Thanks — talk soon,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood + Finovate — stakeholder mapping & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciated the summary. Quick answers: 

Stakeholders (initial):
- Economic buyer: Alex Johnson (me) — will sponsor but CFO will sign off (I’ll introduce once we have numbers)
- Procurement: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@finovatebank.com> (loops in contracts)
- Security: Brian Lee <brian.lee@finovatebank.com> (application security)
- Legal: likely routed via procurement (Sonia)

Timeline:
- Procurement starts: target for Q1 2027 proof-of-concept procurement window; procurement wants estimates & standard SOW by mid-Dec
- Security review: Brian will want SOC 2 and an architecture diagram; likely 2–3 week turnaround once we provide docs

Requests from their side: 
- Can you send SOC 2 summary and an architecture diagram showing data flow (where data resides, encryption in transit/at rest)?
- A short one-page that my executive can read showing expected ROI / cost offsets would help me get internal buy-in

Looping in Sonia and Brian to keep this coordinated.

—Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Data Products, Finovate Bank
alex.johnson@finovatebank.com | +1 312-555-0147

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finovatebank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@finovatebank.com>, Brian Lee <brian.lee@finovatebank.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood + Finovate — stakeholder mapping & champion enablement

Alex / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are the items you requested and a first-pass champion enablement pack: SOC2-summary.pdf, customer-architecture-diagram.png, and champion-talk-track.docx. Highlights below for Sonia / Brian:

- SOC 2: our most recent audit (summary attached). We store customer data in US regions only; encryption at rest via KMS and TLS 1.2+ in transit. Full report available under NDA.
- Architecture: high-level diagram attached showing request flow, KV cache, and optional VPC/private deployment for on-prem or VPC peering.

Champion enablement snippets (for Alex to use with execs):
- 30s elevator: "Redwood Inference provides predictable, low-latency LLM inference with SLA-backed options and cost controls—turning manual review workflows into scalable automated flows while preserving control over data residency and security."
- ROI talk-track:
  - Baseline: current manual review cogs = ~$45k/month for team handling 50k reviews
  - Redwood POC estimate: automation + human-in-the-loop reduces manual reviews by 60% => estimated run-rate savings ~$27k/month plus faster time-to-decision and lower fraud losses
  - Unit economics: based on your ~600k queries/month profile, expected $X–$Y per 1M tokens (we’ll provide exact pricing in the quote)

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll draft a one-page exec summary + mutual action plan for procurement (see attached template).
2) If helpful, schedule a 30-min security sync with Brian to walk through architecture and SOC 2 details — I can join.

Let me know any edits and I’ll revise.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: Redwood + Finovate — stakeholder mapping & champion enablement (internal)

Marissa / Aditya — quick internal note on the enablement packet:

- Marissa: for the exec one-pager, can you include 2 ROI scenarios (conservative / aggressive) with clear assumptions (manual reviews reduced %, time savings, estimated reduction in fraud losses)? Finance will need tangible numbers for CFO.
- Also include estimated timeline and gating items for procurement (SOC2 NDA, contract lead times).
- I can prepare a short cost breakdown by model option (hosted vs dedicated vs private) so Alex can see tradeoffs for Q1 POC vs long-term committed capacity.

I’ll drop the cost table and model comparison by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
